title: Co-cultivation Protocol for Transforming Wheat Stripe Rust
author: Yiheng Hu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f9tbr6n

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium overnight culture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the overnight Agrobacterium tumefaciens culture at 5000×g for 10 min, wash the pellet once with induction media (IM containing glucose), and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL IM (with glucose).

steps.title: Induce Agrobacterium to OD0.6
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL Agro‑IM solution to 8 mL liquid IM (with glucose) in a 50 mL Falcon tube, incubate at 28 °C with shaking until the culture reaches OD₆₀₀ = 0.6 (approximately 6 h, depending on strain).

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend Agrobacterium
steps.instruction: When the IM‑Agrobacterium culture reaches OD₆₀₀ = 0.6, centrifuge at room temperature at 5000×g for 10 min and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL liquid IM (without glucose) supplemented with 200 µM acetosyringone (AS).

steps.title: Harvest and quantify Pst spores
steps.instruction: Harvest fresh Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) spores from previously infected wheat, suspend them in 0.1 % (v/v) Triton X‑100, perform 1:10, 1:100 and 1:1000 dilutions, count spores with a haemocytometer, and estimate that 10 mg (≈20 mL) of spores corresponds to 3.5 × 10⁶ spores.

steps.title: Spread spores on glass plate
steps.instruction: Dust 100 µL of the spore suspension onto a 14 cm‑diameter glass plate or beaker, gently spray water to distribute spores evenly, cover with parafilm, and incubate at 8 °C for ~6 h.

steps.title: Prepare IM‑Agar plates with filters
steps.instruction: Take four IM‑Agar plates containing 200 µM AS, remove them from the 8 °C incubator, use sterilized tweezers to place cut Hybond N⁺ filter strips (five strips per plate) onto the spore layer, dry the filters with hood airflow for 1 min, and position the filter spore‑side up on the agar. Use two plates per pot (≈15 wheat seedlings per pot).

steps.title: Add Agrobacterium suspension to filters
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of IM (no glucose, 200 µM AS) containing Agrobacterium onto each filter with spores, allow the droplets to dry for 3 min, then incubate the plates at 20 °C for 36 h to allow co‑cultivation.

steps.title: Co‑culture filters with wheat seedlings
steps.instruction: After the 36 h co‑cultivation, remove the plates and have 6–8 pots of 9‑day‑old wheat seedlings ready. Gently spray water onto each filter, attach the filter (spore side down) onto the primary leaf of each seedling, spray the plants lightly, and place them in a container with 100 % humidity at 8 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Incubate seedlings in growth chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer the infected wheat seedlings to a growth chamber set to 17 °C, 16 h light / 8 h dark cycle, and 60 % relative humidity.

steps.title: Assess infection and amplify spores
steps.instruction: Eight days later, examine the wheat for spore infection, remove the filter papers to allow pustules to erupt, and plant eight additional pots of wheat to amplify the transformed spores for selection.

steps.title: Collect spores for downstream analysis
steps.instruction: Collect the newly produced spores, and use a small aliquot to reinfect wheat for further analyses such as GUS staining and DNA extraction.
